text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yes, fine. Hello. I'm Jibin.
A: Neil. I'm in Basingstoke.
B: Bradley Stoke, near Bristol.
A: Right. Er, I saw the engineering books behind you. I had a guess you might be in the trade.
B: Yes. Systems engineer, embedded software, aerospace. Filton. And you? You look like an engineer as well, to be honest. The ring binders.
A: Ha. Yeah, guilty. Civil. I'm with the water company, I look after pumping stations and sewers round north Hampshire.
B: Okay. Chartered?
A: Yeah, ICE. Did it in my late twenties. Been at the same place nineteen years now.
B: Nineteen years. That's a long time in one place, actually. I'm chartered too, but IET. In my area people move around a lot more, contracting, competitors. The day rates are very good. I've thought about it, but my wife's job is here, the kids' schools, so basically I stay.
A: Yeah. I've been offered the move up a couple of times, into senior management. Turned it down both times. I didn't fancy the meetings.
B: Really? Both times?
A: Both times. I like knowing where everything is. Somebody rings up and says there's a problem at such-and-such a pump station, and I can sort of picture it, I know which valve's been playing up for ten years. You lose that when you go upstairs.
B: Hm. Fair enough. For me it's the opposite, to be honest. I want principal engineer, technical lead. I think I'm overdue for it. But it's not management exactly, it's still technical, you're still close to the work.
A: That sounds a better deal than what I was offered.
B: Hopefully. What's the software side like in water? Is it all SCADA, old systems?
A: Er, it's a mix. Some of the telemetry's ancient. There are outstations still running on kit older than my son. Consultants come in every few years with a new platform, and we end up keeping half the old stuff anyway.
B: Yes, consultants. Same everywhere. They make a nice slide deck and then leave.
A: That's about it, yeah.
B: Do you follow cricket at all?
A: I do, actually. Test matches mostly. I'll have it on in the garage.
B: Okay, good. I'm India, obviously. I watch on my phone at very strange hours. My wife is not happy about it.
A: Were you up for the last series?
B: Some of it. Four a.m. once, for the last session. To be honest the England batting was a bit, er, reckless. Very attacking, but no plan B.
A: Ha. I'd probably agree with you there. It's exciting until it isn't.
B: Exactly. Exciting until it isn't. I go to Taunton sometimes, Somerset, with a couple of friends. It's a nice ground.
A: I've not been. I'm more of a sofa man for cricket. Football I'll go, Reading, the odd home game.
B: Reading. Are they doing okay?
A: No. Lost again on Saturday.
B: Sorry to hear that.
A: That's all right. You sort of get used to it.
B: Is that your children in the photo? Graduation?
A: Yeah. Daughter and son. Both moved out now. Daughter's a physio, son's at Nottingham finishing up.
B: Good. Mine are twelve and nine, so I still have a long way to go. My son wants a gaming PC. I'm specifying the parts myself.
A: I'd do the same, to be fair. Make sure it's—
